svg.title: The paediatric assessment triangle
svg.desc: A triangle with one assessment arm on each side, formed from the doorway without equipment and before touching the child. Top: APPEARANCE, asking whether the brain is perfused and oxygenated, assessed by TICLS - Tone, Interactiveness, Consolability, Look or gaze, Speech or cry. Bottom left: WORK OF BREATHING - stridor, grunting and wheeze; tripoding, sniffing position and refusing to lie down; retractions; nasal flaring; head bobbing in infants. Bottom right: CIRCULATION TO THE SKIN - pallor, mottling and cyanosis. A warning beside the appearance arm states that the quiet child is the trap: a screaming child is spending energy and interacting, and a floppy silent child who does not mind a stranger is usually the sicker one. A table below gives the four patterns: breathing abnormal alone is respiratory distress; breathing and appearance abnormal is respiratory failure; appearance and skin abnormal with normal breathing is shock; all three abnormal is cardiopulmonary failure.
svg.text: Formed from the doorway. No equipment, no touching, a few seconds.
Is the brain perfused and oxygenated?
Look or gaze · Speech or cry
Position: tripoding · sniffing · will not lie down
What the periphery looks like when the core is prioritised.
→ RESPIRATORY FAILURE — compensation is going. Act now
→ SHOCK — a perfusion problem rather than an airway one
→ CARDIOPULMONARY FAILURE — nothing about this waits
A child not behaving like a child is a sick child, whatever the numbers say. Confirm against your own text.
